title: Projectile motion
competency: Describe horizontal and inclined projectile motion and solve problems on time of flight, range and maximum height.

keywords.def: An object in flight that moves only under gravity after it is thrown or launched.
The path a projectile follows. Without air resistance it is a parabola.
The angle θ between the launch velocity and the horizontal.
The time a projectile spends in the air.
The horizontal distance a projectile covers before it lands at launch level.
The greatest height above the launch level, reached when the vertical velocity is zero.

en.text: A projectile moves under gravity only. Its horizontal velocity stays constant; vertically it falls with acceleration g. A body thrown horizontally from height h lands after t = √(2h/g), the same time as a body dropped from rest, and travels Δx = v₀t.

am.text: ተወንጫፊ በስበት ብቻ ይንቀሳቀሳል። አግድም ፍጥነቱ አይለወጥም፤ ቁልቁል በ g ይወድቃል። ከ h ከፍታ በአግድም የተወረወረ ነገር በ t = √(2h/g) ያርፋል።

screens.title: Dropped or thrown?
screens.ask: From the same height, Abebe drops one stone and throws another straight out sideways at the same moment. Which lands first?
opts: It depends on the stones' mass
screens.after:
They land together.
Both start with zero vertical velocity and fall with the same g.
The sideways speed does not change the fall: the motions are independent.

screens.title: What is a projectile?
paras: A projectile is thrown or launched, then moves under gravity only.
A kicked football, a bullet and a jet of water are projectiles.
We assume: g = 9.8 m/s², always downward.
We ignore air resistance.
So the horizontal velocity stays constant.
The horizontal and vertical motions are independent. They share the same time t.
The path, or trajectory, is a parabola.

screens.title: Horizontal projection
paras: The body leaves with horizontal velocity v₀ and no vertical velocity.
Down is taken as positive here.
screens.note: Time of flight from height h: t = √(2h/g). Range: R = v₀√(2h/g).

screens.title: Throw from a cliff
screens.ask: Change the height and the launch speed. Watch the landing distance.
screens.note: Change only v₀: the time stays the same. The time of flight depends only on h. g = 9.8 m/s².

screens.title: Worked example: a stone from a cliff
steps: Given: h = 80 m, v₀ = 25 m/s horizontal, g = 10 m/s².
Landing velocity parts: vₓ = 25 m/s, v_y = gt = 40 m/s.
Common trap: using v₀ to find the time. The time depends only on h.

screens.title: Key words
defs: An object in flight that moves only under gravity after it is thrown or launched.
The path a projectile follows. Without air resistance it is a parabola.

screens.text: Horizontal projection: a rescue plane flies level and drops a food package. Ignoring air, where is the plane when the package lands?
screens.why:
The package leaves with the plane's horizontal velocity.
No horizontal force acts, so that velocity stays the same.
Plane and package move sideways together.
So the plane is directly above the package when it lands.
Trap: "far behind" assumes the package slows down sideways.
screens.clue: What happens to the horizontal velocity of the package?

screens.ask: Time of flight, horizontal projection: a package is dropped from a plane 300 m high (g = 10 m/s²). It reaches the ground after ≈ ___ s (2 decimal places)
screens.why:
Formula: h = ½gt², so t = √(2h/g).
Substitute: t = √(2 × 300 m ÷ 10 m/s²).
t = √60 s² = 7.75 s.
Trap: the plane's speed does not change the fall time.
(The book truncates to 7.74 s.)
screens.clue: Use h = ½gt² with no starting vertical velocity.

screens.ask: Horizontal distance: the plane flies at 360 km/h. It must release the package ≈ ___ m before it is over the driver (nearest metre)
screens.why:
Convert: 360 km/h ÷ 3.6 = 100 m/s.
Formula: Δx = v₀t, with t = 7.75 s from the fall.
Substitute: Δx = 100 m/s × 7.75 s.
Result: Δx ≈ 775 m (book: 774 m).
Trap: using 360 without converting gives a huge, wrong answer.
screens.clue: Change km/h to m/s first, then use Δx = v₀t.

screens.ask: Time of flight, horizontal projection: a ball is thrown horizontally at 20 m/s from a building 90 m high (g = 10 m/s²). Time of flight ≈ ___ s (2 decimal places)
screens.why:
Formula: t = √(2h/g). Only the height decides the time.
Substitute: t = √(2 × 90 ÷ 10) = √18.
Result: t ≈ 4.24 s.
Trap: the 20 m/s is not used for the time.
screens.clue: Only the height decides the time.

screens.ask: Horizontal distance: same ball (20 m/s, t = 4.24 s). It lands ≈ ___ m from the foot of the building (nearest metre)
screens.why:
Formula: Δx = v₀t.
The horizontal speed stays 20 m/s the whole time.
Substitute: Δx = 20 m/s × 4.24 s = 84.9 m.
Result: ≈ 85 m.
screens.clue: Horizontal speed stays 20 m/s.

screens.ask: Landing speed: same ball (vₓ = 20 m/s, t = 4.24 s, g = 10 m/s²). It hits the ground at ≈ ___ m/s (1 decimal place)
screens.why:
Vertical speed: v_y = gt = 10 × 4.24 = 42.4 m/s.
Horizontal speed: vₓ = 20 m/s (unchanged).
Combine with Pythagoras: v = √(vₓ² + v_y²) = √(400 + 1800).
v = √2200 ≈ 46.9 m/s.
Trap: adding 20 + 42.4 is wrong; the parts are at right angles.
screens.clue: Combine vₓ and v_y with Pythagoras.

screens.ask: Bullet drop: a gun with muzzle speed 500 m/s aims at a target 50 m away (g = 10 m/s²). To hit it, aim ≈ ___ cm above the target
screens.why:
Time to reach the target: t = Δx/v₀ = 50 ÷ 500 = 0.1 s.
In that time the bullet falls: Δy = ½gt² = ½ × 10 × 0.1².
Δy = 0.05 m = 5 cm.
So aim 5 cm above the target.
screens.clue: Find the time to reach the target first.

en.text: A body launched at angle θ has v₀ₓ = v₀cosθ and v₀y = v₀sinθ. The horizontal velocity stays v₀cosθ. Vertically v_y = v₀sinθ − gt, so it rises, stops rising at the top and falls back. Time to the top is v₀sinθ/g; over level ground the time of flight is 2v₀sinθ/g.

am.text: በማዕዘን θ የተወረወረ ነገር v₀cosθ አግድም፣ v₀sinθ ቁልቁል ፍጥነት አለው። ከፍተኛ ቦታ ላይ v_y = 0 ነው። የበረራ ጊዜ 2v₀sinθ/g ነው።

screens.title: At the very top
screens.ask: A football is kicked up at an angle. At the highest point of its path, what is true?
screens.after:
At the top only the vertical velocity is zero.
The horizontal velocity v₀cosθ never changes, so the ball still moves sideways.
Gravity never switches off: the acceleration is still g downward.

screens.title: Launching at an angle
paras: Split the launch velocity into two parts.
Horizontal: v₀ₓ = v₀cosθ. It never changes.
Vertical: v₀y = v₀sinθ. Gravity slows it, then reverses it.
screens.note: The book writes +gt and +½gt² with g = −9.8 m/s². Both forms give the same answers.

screens.title: Split the launch velocity
screens.ask: Change the speed and the angle. Watch the two parts.
screens.note: At 0° all the speed is horizontal; at 90° all of it is vertical. g = 9.8 m/s².

screens.title: Time of flight
paras: At the top v_y = 0. So the time to the top is t = v₀sinθ/g.
Over level ground the fall takes the same time.
Time of flight: T = 2v₀sinθ/g.
Use T only when launch and landing are at the same level.

screens.title: A ball kicked toward a wall
steps: v₀ = 25 m/s at 53°, wall 24 m away, g = 10 m/s², cos53° = 0.6, sin53° = 0.8.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The angle θ between the launch velocity and the horizontal.
The time a projectile spends in the air.

screens.text: Inclined projection: at which point of the flight is the speed least?
screens.why:
Speed = √(vₓ² + v_y²).
vₓ is the same everywhere.
v_y is zero only at maximum height.
So the speed is least there: v = vₓ = v₀cosθ.
Trap: the speed is not zero at the top.
screens.clue: Which part of the velocity disappears at the top?

screens.text: Velocity and acceleration at the top, true or false: they are perpendicular at the highest point.
screens.why:
At the top v_y = 0, so the velocity is horizontal.
The acceleration is g, straight down.
Horizontal and vertical are at 90°.
So the statement is true.
screens.clue: Which way does each point at the top?

screens.ask: Launch angle from time to the top: a body launched at 30 m/s reaches its highest point after 1.5 s (g = 10 m/s²). The launch angle is ___°
screens.why:
At the top v_y = 0: v₀sinθ − gt = 0.
So v₀sinθ = gt = 10 × 1.5 = 15 m/s.
sinθ = 15 ÷ 30 = 0.5.
θ = 30°.
screens.clue: At the top v_y = 0: v₀sinθ = gt.

screens.ask: Range from the time of flight: same body (30 m/s at 30°, 1.5 s to the top). Its range is ≈ ___ m (1 decimal place)
screens.why:
Time of flight: T = 2 × 1.5 = 3 s (level ground).
Horizontal speed: vₓ = 30cos30° = 30 × 0.866 = 25.98 m/s.
Range: R = vₓT = 25.98 × 3 = 77.9 m.
Check: R = v₀² sin2θ/g = 900 × 0.866 ÷ 10 = 77.9 m ✓
screens.clue: Total time is twice the time to the top.

screens.text: Projectile facts: which are true for a projectile with no air resistance? Pick all that apply.
pool: Its acceleration is g downward everywhere
Its vertical velocity is zero at the top
Its acceleration is zero at the top
a: Its acceleration is g downward everywhere
Its vertical velocity is zero at the top
screens.why:
No horizontal force acts, so vₓ is constant.
Gravity acts all the time, so the acceleration is g downward everywhere.
At the top v_y = 0.
The acceleration is never zero, not even at the top.
screens.clue: Think about what gravity does at the top.

screens.ask: Launch angle from speeds: a projectile's launch speed is five times its speed at the top. The launch angle is ≈ ___° (1 decimal place)
screens.why:
At the top only vₓ is left: v_top = v₀cosθ.
Given: v₀ = 5 v_top = 5 v₀cosθ.
So cosθ = 1/5 = 0.2.
θ = cos⁻¹(0.2) ≈ 78.5°.
screens.clue: What speed is left at the top?

en.text: Over level ground the range is R = v₀² sin2θ/g and the maximum height is H = v₀² sin²θ/(2g). The range is greatest at 45°, and complementary angles such as 30° and 60° give the same range. A steeper launch always gives a greater height.

am.text: አግድም ርቀት R = v₀² sin2θ/g፣ ከፍተኛ ከፍታ H = v₀² sin²θ/(2g) ነው። በ45° ርቀቱ ትልቁ ነው፤ ተደጋጋፊ ማዕዘኖች እኩል ርቀት ይሰጣሉ።

screens.title: Aim the kick
screens.ask: Change the speed and the angle. Find the angle with the longest range. Compare 30° with 60°.
screens.note: g = 9.8 m/s², level ground. 30° and 60° give the same range, but 60° goes higher and stays up longer.

screens.title: Range and height formulas
paras: Range: R = v₀² sin2θ/g.
The greatest range is at θ = 45°: R_max = v₀²/g.
Angles that add to 90° give the same range.
Maximum height: H = v₀² sin²θ/(2g).
Linking them: H = R tanθ/4.
These need launch and landing at the same level.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The horizontal distance a projectile covers before it lands at launch level.
The greatest height above the launch level, reached when the vertical velocity is zero.

screens.text: Maximum range: which launch angle gives the greatest range over level ground?
screens.why:
Formula: R = v₀² sin2θ/g.
R is largest when sin2θ = 1.
sin2θ = 1 when 2θ = 90°, so θ = 45°.
Then R_max = v₀²/g.
screens.clue: When is sin2θ biggest?

screens.text: Complementary angles: balls A (37°) and B (53°) are kicked with the same speed. Which statement is true?
opts: B goes farther; A goes higher
screens.why:
37° + 53° = 90°, so sin74° = sin106°.
So sin2θ is the same: equal ranges.
H = v₀² sin²θ/(2g) grows with θ.
So the steeper ball B goes higher.
Answer: same range; B goes higher.
screens.clue: Add the two angles.

screens.ask: Maximum height: a ball is kicked at 40 m/s at 37° (g = 10 m/s², sin37° = 0.6). Maximum height H = ___ m
screens.why:
Formula: H = v₀² sin²θ/(2g).
Substitute: H = 40² × 0.6² ÷ (2 × 10).
H = 1600 × 0.36 ÷ 20 = 576 ÷ 20.
Result: H = 28.8 m.
Trap: forgetting to square sinθ gives 48 m.
screens.clue: Square sin37° before you multiply.

screens.ask: Range: same kick (40 m/s at 37°, sin74° = 0.96, g = 10 m/s²). Range R ≈ ___ m (nearest metre)
screens.why:
Formula: R = v₀² sin2θ/g.
2θ = 74°, so sin2θ = 0.96.
Substitute: R = 1600 × 0.96 ÷ 10 = 153.6 m.
Result: ≈ 154 m (book 153.8 m).
Trap: using sin37° instead of sin74° gives 96 m.
screens.clue: Use sin2θ, not sinθ.

screens.text: Range and height: the range of a projectile is 3 times its maximum height. The launch angle is about
screens.why:
Link: H = R tanθ/4, so tanθ = 4H/R.
Given R = 3H: tanθ = 4H/(3H) = 4/3.
θ = tan⁻¹(4/3) ≈ 53°.
Check: at 45°, R = 4H, not 3H.
screens.clue: Use H = R tanθ/4.

screens.text: Range on the Moon (g ≈ 1.6 m/s²): the same launch made on the Moon has a range, compared with Earth,
screens.why:
Formula: R = v₀² sin2θ/g, so R ∝ 1/g.
Ratio: 9.8 ÷ 1.6 ≈ 6.
So the range is about 6 times greater.
H ∝ 1/g too, so it is also about 6 times greater.
screens.clue: g is in the denominator.

screens.ask: Long jump range: a jumper leaves the ground at 11.0 m/s and 20.0° (sin40° = 0.643, g = 10 m/s²). Jump length ≈ ___ m (1 decimal place)
screens.why:
Treat as level ground: R = v₀² sin2θ/g.
2θ = 40°, sin40° = 0.643.
Substitute: R = 11.0² × 0.643 ÷ 10 = 121 × 0.643 ÷ 10.
Result: R ≈ 7.8 m.
screens.clue: Treat the jump as level ground: R = v₀² sin2θ/g.

items.text: Exercise 2.1 Q2, aiming a gun: muzzle speed 500 m/s, target 50 m away. To hit it, the gun should be aimed
items.why:
Time to target: t = 50 ÷ 500 = 0.1 s.
Drop: Δy = ½gt² = ½ × 10 × 0.01 = 0.05 m.
The bullet falls 5 cm, so aim 5 cm above.
Trap: aiming straight at it misses low.
items.clue: How far does the bullet fall on the way?

items.ask: Exercise 2.1 Q4 b, long jump height: (11.0 m/s, 20.0°, g = 10 m/s², sin20° = 0.342). The jumper rises ≈ ___ m (2 decimal places)
items.why:
Formula: H = v₀² sin²θ/(2g).
sin²20° = 0.342² = 0.117.
Substitute: H = 121 × 0.117 ÷ 20.
Result: H ≈ 0.71 m.

test.ask: Time of flight, horizontal throw: a stone is thrown horizontally at 15 m/s from a 20 m cliff (g = 10 m/s²). It lands after ___ s
test.why:
Formula: t = √(2h/g).
Substitute: t = √(2 × 20 ÷ 10) = √4.
Result: t = 2 s.
The 15 m/s does not change the fall time.

test.ask: Horizontal distance: same stone (15 m/s, 2 s in the air). It lands ___ m from the foot of the cliff
test.why:
Formula: Δx = v₀t.
Substitute: Δx = 15 m/s × 2 s.
Result: 30 m.

test.text: Complementary angles: which angle gives the same range as 30° for the same speed?
test.why:
Angles that add to 90° give the same range.
90° − 30° = 60°.
Check: sin60° = sin120°.

test.ask: Range: a ball is kicked at 20 m/s at 45° (g = 10 m/s²). Range R = ___ m
test.why:
Formula: R = v₀² sin2θ/g.
sin90° = 1.
R = 400 × 1 ÷ 10 = 40 m.

test.ask: Maximum height: a ball is kicked at 20 m/s at 30° (g = 10 m/s²). H = ___ m
test.why:
Formula: H = v₀² sin²θ/(2g).
sin30° = 0.5, so sin²30° = 0.25.
H = 400 × 0.25 ÷ 20 = 5 m.
Trap: forgetting to square gives 10 m.

notes.text: Example 2.1: t = √0.004 = 0.0632 s; using it gives v₀ ≈ 474 m/s, not 500 m/s (the book rounds t to 0.06 s too early).
Example 2.2: √60 = 7.746 s ≈ 7.75 s and Δx ≈ 775 m (book truncates to 7.74 s, 774 m). The package must be released 774–775 m BEFORE the driver.
Example 2.3: denominator printed as 10 m/s; should be 10 m/s². R = 153.6 m with sin74° = 0.96 or 153.8 m with 0.961.
Sign of g: the book writes v_y = v₀sinθ + gt and Δy = v₀sinθ t + ½gt² with g = −9.8 m/s². Lessons use up-positive with −gt and −½gt² (g = +9.8). Teachers should point out both forms.
Exercise 2.1 Q3 and Q4 answers use g = 10 m/s² (Q4 with 9.8 gives R ≈ 7.94 m, H ≈ 0.722 m). The questions state g = 10 m/s².
Activities 2.1–2.4 (table-top launches) are hands-on and are not turned into graded items.
